reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds shared predicates isWeekendOrHoliday/isDailyWeekendSkip, but getNextDate re-checks frequency === 'daily' inline instead of using isDailyWeekendSkip, and the new range handler rebuilds the getUpcomingDates pipeline rather than sharing it.

duplication.why: The filter-daily-weekends + move-weekend map pipeline is copied between getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, the daily predicate is spelled three ways, and schedule-template repeats its moveWeekend getDateWithSkippedWeekend block twice.

placement.why: Weekend/holiday rules live in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in server/schedules/app.ts, consistent with the tree's layering.

scope.why: Changes are on-task across the four steps; release notes added; no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: Holiday stepping loop in one helper is clean, but the occurrence-adjust pipeline exists in several hand-written variants (getNextDate, two handlers, schedule-template with an opaque `moveWeekend || !skipWeekend` flag), so the next rule change must be applied in four places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getNextDate checks value.schedule.data.frequency === 'daily' inline instead of isDailyWeekendSkip; getDatesInRange re-implements getUpcomingDates' skip/move pipeline instead of a shared 'adjusted occurrences' function

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange copies getUpcomingDates' filter/map chain with a widened window and extra range filter; daily-skip predicate reshaped as isDailyWeekendSkip, inline frequency check in getNextDate, and moveWeekend in schedule-template.ts

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily early-return branch and a frequency !== 'daily' guard; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template.ts each decide skip-vs-move themselves around the helper
